title: Limb dominant vs Torso dominant: does it matter?
summary: He breaks down what torso or limb dominance could objectively mean (insertions, proportions, muscle bellies). He argues the label is mostly an excuse for small arms produced by powerlifting-style training. Arms grow when trained with the same progressive, high-intensity approach used for squats and bench.
claims: Torso and limb dominant are recent YouTube terms, a sign the concept is not fleshed out
Objectively, torso dominance could mean good chest insertions, a thick ribcage, clavicle length or a propensity to develop torso muscles
A short torso with long legs makes muscle look more impressive and 3D even with modest measurements
Short arms with good insertions look big even with unremarkable measurements
With poor triceps insertions, part of the area near the elbow is bare tendon that can never be developed
Muscle belly shape such as a biceps peak or sweep cannot be trained in; even surgically reattaching a torn biceps lower never looks right
The labels are too vague: one torso-dominant person has a barrel chest but weak back, another big lats but small traps
People use torso dominant to excuse small arms; defining yourself by your weaknesses rather than your strengths is a bad approach
Torso mass comes simply from heavy compounds like rows, pull-ups, bench and presses that everyone already does; arms are more complicated
The epidemic of torso-dominant lifters comes from powerlifting-style programs: bench hits chest, front delts and the shorter triceps heads, deadlifts grow the back, neither grows the arms
At 18 he was torso dominant, a torso with two spaghetti arms, because of short clavicles; years of heavy curls in his room later made his arms bigger than his shoulders and chest
There is no fatality: training environment, not genetics, largely decides whether you are torso or limb dominant, and you can transition
Powerlifters gain nothing from being arm dominant, but a bodybuilder with small arms is not really viable
Naturals have big quads because they squat with high intensity and tonnage, yet train biceps with 3x10 hammer curls after bench
To grow arms, train them with high intensity, strict form and frequency, and progressively overload a heavy biceps and a heavy triceps movement
Heavy cheat curls with an EZ bar, chin-ups and 75 sets of light stuff are not the way to big arms
exercises: 3x10 after bench is not enough to grow biceps
